Subject: MAP + acceptance tests for pilot

Hi Evelyn / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at BrightCare is aligned on a short pilot (6 weeks) to validate inference quality and integration overhead. Before we lock in dates, procurement asked for a clear Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with concrete acceptance tests and the signoff flow so they can budget headcount and QA cycles.

Two asks from our side:
- A concise exit-gate list (what would cause BrightCare NOT to go to prod)
- Concrete acceptance tests we can run against a staging endpoint (we need examples and pass thresholds)

Can you drop a one-page MAP + test list we can share with procurement by EOD Wednesday? Also include any required SOC2 / security artifacts we should request.

Best,
Sara

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@brightcare.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:45:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance tests for pilot

Sara — thanks, copying a draft MAP and the acceptance scripts for your procurement and QA teams. High level: we break the MAP into three lanes (technical verification, security/compliance, commercial milestones) with clear owner and expected artifact for each date. Key acceptance criteria we recommend for the pilot:

- Model correctness / quality: intent-match > 92% on your labeled 1k sample set; top-1 response precision > 90% for transactional prompts.
- Hallucination tolerance: < 1.5% of sampled responses flagged as hallucinations by independent reviewers (sample size 500).
- Latency: 95th percentile latency (inference only) < 300ms for standard prompt profile; 99th percentile < 700ms.
- Throughput: sustain 25 requests/sec with P95 latency target preserved in our canary harness.
- Availability: < 1% error rate over 24h rolling windows during test runs.
- Privacy/safety: PII redaction verified on 200 known PII prompts; data retention policy confirmed (30-day log retention for pilot; option to disable logs).

Exit gates (immediate stop to go-live):
- Any open P0 bug in core inference path impacting >5% of requests or causing data exfiltration risk.
- Failure to provide SOC2 Type II attestation or equivalent evidence requested in >5 business days.
- Inability to meet encryption/retention controls required by your security team.
- Model quality regression where intent-match drop > 6 points vs baseline.

Acceptance tests included (attached file 'acceptance-scripts.md'):
1) Functional: 1k labeled scenarios run; pass if precision/recall meets thresholds.
2) Adversarial: 200 adversarial prompts to check hallucination and safety filters.
3) Load: step-load to 40 RPS sustained for 5m, verify P95 < 300ms.
4) Integration: 50 end-to-end flows via your API gateway to validate headers, auth, and payload size handling.
5) Audit/logs: confirm presence of trace-id on 100 sampled requests and verify logs show appropriate fields.

Rollout plan: canary (10% traffic) for 48h -> 50% for 5 days -> full cutover pending signoff. Each step has a 24-hour hold for metric review.

I've attached: BrightCare_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP lanes + owners), acceptance-scripts.md (tests + runbook), and a load-test template. Please review and tell me if procurement needs additional wording.

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:05:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance tests for pilot

Looping in a couple of engineering specifics we should call out explicitly in the MAP so QA knows how to run tests and reproduce results:

- Test harness notes: our canary harness will pin a KV-cache warm-up phase (200 warm prompts) before measuring latency to avoid cold-start noise. Please instruct BrightCare to include the same warm-up in their runs.
- Determinism: for scoring, we will run each prompt 3x (random seed fixed) and use the mode response where applicable — this avoids flakiness for conversational prompts.
- Regression measurement: provide a snapshot baseline (we recommend running the 1k labeled set against your current system and our staging endpoint; we will compute delta intent-match).
- Fallback behavior: if P95 latency > 300ms for >10% of intervals during a 1h window, traffic will fall back to a lower-capacity model variant; that fallback counts as an operational failure if it persists >2h without remediation.

Also note: for SOC2 artifacts, security will provide our SOC2 summary and a list of required evidence (we can't share the full report externally without an NDA; procurement often accepts an AICPA bridge letter + SOC2 summary).

If you OK these items I will add the two runbook steps to the acceptance-scripts.md (warm-up, fixed-seed run).

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- QA: will run the 1k labeled set and the adversarial script. Can you confirm you will share a runbook command-line (curl/example client) that sets the warm-up seed and captures trace-ids?
- Security: they want the PII redaction test details (we'll run the provided 200 PII prompts).

Next step: can we lock a technical kickoff with engineering this Thursday 12pm PT? If that works I'll send an invite.

Assuming the kickoff goes well, procurement is OK to sign the SOW contingent on the MAP artifacts above and a final go/no-go at the end of week 3 of the pilot.
